facts.content: Patient has a 3-day history of watery diarrhea occurring 5-6 times per day.
Onset with 2 episodes of vomiting which have resolved.
No blood in stool.
No abdominal pain.
Feels dehydrated.
Poor oral intake and low appetite.
Felt febrile early on but is now afebrile.
facts.source_text: felt febrile early on, now afebrile

facts.content: Reports weakness.
No headache or myalgias.
No known sick contacts and no suspect food.
facts.source_text: no known sick contacts; no suspect food

facts.content: Patient has a history of asthma.
Uses a blue inhaler as needed.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Father had bowel cancer and hypertension.
Mother has type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Patient lives alone and is a software engineer.
Off work for 3 days due to illness.
facts.source_text: off work x3 days due to illness

facts.content: Drinks alcohol socially and is a non-smoker.
Acute gastroenteritis with dehydration risk, likely self-limited viral.
facts.source_text: Acute gastroenteritis with dehydration risk — 3 days watery diarrhea, prior brief vomiting, no blood, minimal PO, weakness; likely self-limited viral

facts.content: Encourage clear fluids and oral rehydration solution as directed.
facts.source_text: ORT: Encourage clear fluids; oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) as directed

facts.content: Symptomatic treatment with paracetamol as needed for fever or aches; rest is advised.
Diet: Gradual oral intake as tolerated; avoid dairy, caffeine, and alcohol; small frequent sips then bland foods.
facts.source_text: Diet: Gradual PO as tolerated; avoid dairy/caffeine/alcohol; small frequent sips then bland foods

facts.content: Patient advised to remain off work until diarrhea-free for 24 to 48 hours.
Return precautions include persistent symptoms for more than 5–7 days, high fever, worsening weakness, signs of dehydration, bloody stools, severe abdominal pain, or inability to keep fluids.
facts.source_text: Return/ED precautions: Persistent sx >5–7 days; high fever, worsening weakness, signs of dehydration (oliguria, dizziness), bloody stools, severe abd pain, inability to keep fluids

facts.content: Patient should follow up if not improving by next week for re-evaluation.
facts.source_text: Follow-up: If not improving by next week, re-evaluate
